reasons: The cited Section 11.3 contains only a mutual return-or-destroy of Confidential Information with no format, timescale, certification, or transition-assistance right, so it does not reach the fallback (90 days assistance; export within 30 days); classifying this as a missing clause requiring insertion is correct.

The inserted Section 11.4 is directionally correct for us as the customer-side party (Corio): it imposes the transition, return, deletion and certification duties on Commerce One as vendor/host, and tracks the preferred position (6 months at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, deletion plus written certification).

Edit is minimal and non-destructive — the original paragraph is left intact and a new subsection is appended in the termination section, with a sensible carve-back for Commerce One's surviving Section 11.3 obligations and legal retention so it does not conflict with the existing run-off rights.
Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, in first person plural, states what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.
